answer: The system assigns each new AI node a cryptographic proof anchored to a unique physical landmark model – for example a simulated karst formation – and records its position as a vertex in a distributed ledger. When a node answers a grading query, it must also submit a honeypot response tied to a neighboring knoll reference; mismatches trigger automatic revocation. An attacker must forge both the landmark proof and the synchronized honeypot answer for every vertex, raising the cost to O(n) cryptographic operations and network fees, which scales prohibitively with the size of the fake swarm.
